2026-10-16 · S2THE COUGH THAT FOLLOWED THE BELLSKAŠELJ, KI JE SLEDIL ZVONOVOM90

Forty-one children cough every Sunday night in a mountain town that has spent five weeks blaming its doctors and its church, and nobody has asked which bell, which room, or what changed last winter.

01 · Forty-One Notebooks

Children's clinic, Ostrava Vell · Monday, 07:40

Ostrava Vell was a mountain town of four thousand people, one church with a tower too large for it, and, since the second week of September, forty-one children who coughed in the evenings.

Dr. Ilse Varga had taped her spirometry curves to the examination-room wall, one line to a child. Every line sagged on Sunday night and climbed back by Thursday, forty-one small tides.

Ilse VargaCultures, PCR, serology, three rounds. There is nothing in any of them. No virus I know keeps a calendar.

Judit Moravec, who chaired the town council, had come in with her coat on. Father Matej Hroch of St. Wenzel stood by the door with his hands in his sleeves.

Judit MoravecThe council wants the school shut on Wednesday. A closed school is a thing I can actually do. Tell me what else I can do by Wednesday.

Matej HrochWhile you look for something to shut, leave the bells out of it. This town blamed them for the hail and the winter the cows failed. They were innocent every time.

Illuminara stood before the curves, then before the map beside them, where each child was a pin in the street they lived on and the pins thickened toward the church.

IlluminaraEveryone has plotted the children by where they live. Has anyone plotted them by where they sleep?

Ilse VargaWhere they sleep is where they live.

IlluminaraUsually.

Nives Hadzic had come in with her coat still buttoned. She held out a school exercise book, soft at the corners.

Nives HadzicForty-one mothers, forty-one notebooks. I write down every cough, the hour, and where she slept that night. And Lenka does not fit. We are out on Spindle Road, past the cemetery, the farthest house from the tower there is. She coughs on Sundays like the rest of them.

Ilse VargaI set Lenka aside as an outlier.

Illuminara turned the pages. Saturday: to Baba's on Cooper's Lane. Sunday: home at five. Sunday night: coughing, two hours.

IlluminaraCooper's Lane is right under the tower. Then she is not an outlier. She is the one child you have who proves something. The cough follows the child and not the address, so it is not a street, and probably not a germ going door to door. It is a room she slept in, and the room has a clock.

The doctors had asked what was in the children. Nobody had asked what was in the rooms.

IlluminaraTell me where each of them slept on Saturday night.

02 · Saint's Flour

St. Wenzel's tower, ringing chamber · Monday, 10:15

Dana Kral had pulled the bells of St. Wenzel for thirty-eight years, as her husband had before her, and she watched the stranger look at the ropes instead of the bells and made ready to be annoyed.

IlluminaraI have one question, and I think nobody has asked it. Which bell is the heaviest, and when is it rung?

Dana KralEverybody asks which is loudest.

IlluminaraI am not asking about loud.

Dana KralOld Wenzel, two tonnes and a hundred kilos. Four of us swing him, Sundays and feast days only. The little ones go from the keyboard, and the hour bells strike by the clock every day.

Matej HrochThere, you see. The hour bells strike every day and nobody coughs on a Tuesday.

IlluminaraI agree. So it is not the bells. It may be one bell, on one day.

She asked for a single stroke of the old bell. Hroch looked a long time at the rope, and allowed exactly one. Dana and three ringers swung Old Wenzel up, and Illuminara went down and stood on the flagstones at the west wall.

The stroke came through the tower like a blow to the bottom of a chair. The tower pressed its weight into the stone, the stone passed it down, and she read where the paths ran. Under the west wall they stopped. There the rock carried nothing and only hung, a long emptiness with a thin roof, and it answered the stroke the way a drumhead answers a palm.

Something down there rings.

IlluminaraUnder this wall there is a hollow, wide and shallow. When Old Wenzel strikes, its ceiling moves.

Matej HrochThe tower stands on rock.

Dana KralIt stands on the lip of the old adit. The miners' air shaft, bricked and boarded before my grandmother's time. Mind the floor by the lectern, it is hollow.

She pushed back her sleeve. Along the dark wool lay a fine white powder, like flour.

Dana KralSaint's flour. It comes up between the boards on every feast day. My grandmother said it was Wenzel blessing our hands.

IlluminaraThen it is not new. Something else is.

Emil RaskI can tell you what is new.

The chimney sweep had come up the stairs behind them with his apprentice and a bag of rods. He was sixty-eight and filled the doorway.

Emil RaskLast winter's grant. I did sixty-three chimneys for it in the old quarter. New stoves, sealed windows, no draught, less coal. A house with its windows shut drinks from its cellar.

03 · Two Mouths

Cooper's Lane, cellars of the old quarter · Tuesday, 14:00

Emil Rask had one rule for entering a cellar and he gave it on every doorstep: the tenant says yes, or the rods stay in the bag.

Eleven of the twelve said yes. Alois Fenner, at number nine, stood in his doorway with his arms folded.

Alois FennerMy father's cellar and his father's. Nobody counts my air.

Emil RaskThen I cannot map it, Alois. Not without you.

Alois FennerThen don't.

Illuminara could have found the mouth of that cellar in half a minute. She looked at the folded arms and left it unread. The map would have a gap in it.

In Baba Hadzic's cellar the apprentice, Tilo, who was sixteen and had been told to say nothing, held a smoke pencil to the wall by the coal bin. The thread of smoke leaned toward a bricked arch behind it, where the mortar was thin enough to feel a cold breath through.

TiloIt is pulling in. All of it.

The sweep took the pencil to a grating in the cellar's other wall. The smoke leaned that way too.

Emil RaskTwo mouths. Don't you tell me it is one. The arch feeds this room, and so does the street.

IlluminaraI won't. The street air should be nearly clean and the arch should not, but I cannot claim either until something counts them.

Ilse Varga had arrived with three laser dust counters in a padded case.

Ilse VargaNobody says the word silica in my clinic until a counter says particles.

IlluminaraAgreed. Then a test that can lose. Wednesday at three, when no one is baking and no one is at church. Counters in Baba Hadzic's cellar, the school and down the lane. Ten minutes of the small bells. Then Old Wenzel alone, for ten.

IlluminaraIf the school's counter climbs with Baba's, the dust is everywhere and I am wrong. If the small bells raise Baba's, it is the tower and not the shaft. If Baba's has not at least quadrupled within twenty minutes of the first stroke, I am wrong a third way.

Ilse VargaAnd if you are right, you still do not know what the dust is.

IlluminaraNo. That needs a lab.

Emil RaskAnd I want the grating counted by itself. A counter in the pipe.

IlluminaraYou shall have one.

04 · Wednesday, Out of Season

St. Wenzel's tower and three cellars · Wednesday, 15:00

Nobody could order Old Wenzel rung. Four ringers swung him by their own wish or not at all, and the wish was Dana Kral's.

Dana KralI will ring him on a Wednesday, which I have never done, for ten minutes, which I have never wanted. One telephone call from the clinic with a child's name in it, and I stop on the spot, whatever is on your counters.

Matej HrochAnd I will stand in my tower and watch you do it.

The mothers had decided that no child should be in the old quarter's cellars that afternoon. Ilse Varga read the counters over the telephone from the clinic.

Ilse VargaBaseline, all three: Baba Hadzic's twenty-two, the school nineteen, Cooper's Lane twenty-four. Stoves lit, as on any weekday. Small bells, now.

The five small bells chimed for ten minutes, bright and a little silly.

Ilse VargaTwenty-one. Twenty. Twenty-four. Nothing.

IlluminaraThe small ones are innocent. Dana.

Old Wenzel went up from rest and spoke. The note was lower than anything the ear could hold. It lived in the soles of the feet.

Ilse VargaMinute four. Baba Hadzic's thirty-one. School nineteen.

Between the boards the saint's flour rose in a thin white breath. Dana let the rope settle at ten minutes, as bargained, but the dust in the lane was still on its way, and the counters kept climbing.

Ilse VargaMinute fourteen. A hundred and ninety. School nineteen. Cooper's Lane a hundred and twelve. The pipe from the street grating, twenty-six.

The arch had fed that cellar nearly nine times its ordinary dust, and the street had hardly stirred it.

Matej HrochIt may be my tower's own stone. Limestone dusts. Pigeons. I will not be told it is the shaft until somebody looks at the dust itself.

IlluminaraThat is the right objection.

Ilse VargaThe tower is limestone, and limestone will not hurt a child's lung. Quartz will. If I find quartz in this, it is not your tower. If I find lime and pigeon, I will tell the council the bells were blamed wrongly again, Father, and I will say it from your pulpit if you let me.

Matej HrochI will let you.

05 · One Course of Brick

The old air shaft and the adit beneath the west wall · Thursday, 06:00

Hroch had allowed one course of brick to be lifted from the tower floor, and had asked that it be put back. Under it a shaft a metre wide, plastered smooth, fell into the dark. Emil Rask had put a torch on the timbers below.

Emil RaskThat roof has been rotting since my grandfather's day. Anything that goes down there goes on a rope, and I would be burying it.

IlluminaraI do not need the rope. I do need you on the cable, to read me the counter on my lanyard every ten minutes. If the roof comes down, do not dig. Wait. I will be a while, and I will come back.

She went down into a dark that was a kind of information. The gallery ran a hundred and forty metres under Cooper's Lane, its roof lined with lime plaster and sharp white sand that in places had come away from the rock and hung in sheets. On the floor lay three centimetres of dust the colour of flour. Where she stepped it rose and stayed in the air like a held breath.

IlluminaraEleven hundred where I stand. The arch you smoked is sixty-two metres east. The street grating's branch joins at forty metres and its air is clean, and it carries about a tenth of it, as you said. I will say so at the table.

She took three samples in glass: plaster, floor dust, and a flake of the tower's own limestone. It would have been easy to feel certain. She made herself wait for the lab.

One thing she had not expected: the bell arrived in the gallery as pressure. Every stroke pumped the long tunnel like a bellows, and each pump drove the dust east along the floor toward the arch.

IlluminaraEmil. If you plug that arch, the plug needs a breather: a pipe to the open air, far from any window. Otherwise the bell will press the dust through the old mortar around whatever you build, like water through a sponge.

Emil RaskThat is what a chimney sweep is for, miss. I would have said so in the next minute.

IlluminaraSay it in this one.

Emil RaskA pipe along the cemetery wall, to a stub chimney above the roofline. Thirty metres. Tilo can lay it by Saturday.

Then she worked. The tunnel was too long and too rotten to save in a morning. She read where the plaster would let go first, under the bell's footprint, and there she sprayed a lime-and-casein binder from the hose Tilo fed down the shaft, a skin that would hold until a proper crew came. Eleven metres. It took four hours.

IlluminaraA hundred and twenty-nine metres remain untouched. The worst of it is covered. It is not all of it. I want that written down.

Emil RaskIt is written.

The lab result reached the clinic on Friday morning.

Ilse VargaAngular quartz, three to eight microns, in a lime binder. The same as your gallery plaster. No quartz in the tower limestone. No pigeon. Father, your stone is clean.

06 · The Full Peal

Baba Hadzic's kitchen and the old quarter · Friday, 15:00 to Sunday, 11:00

On Friday Ilse laid the forty-one cards on Baba Hadzic's kitchen table, and Nives, who had written them, moved them about like a woman dealing patience.

Ilse VargaThirty-one of the forty-one slept on Saturday night, or spent Sunday morning, in a room with a mouth to the gallery. Ten did not, and I will not make them fit. Of the fifty-eight in the same classes who do not cough, six were in such rooms: four with grandmothers who air the house all day, and two I cannot explain.

IlluminaraThen what you hold is a strong trigger in the connected rooms. It is not the whole cohort, and it is not a disease.

Ilse VargaI will say exactly that, and not silicosis, for a child who has coughed five Sundays. And if a Sunday comes when the counters stay low and the coughs come anyway, we begin again, and I tell the council so.

Tilo laid the breather pipe along the cemetery wall on Saturday, and Rask's lime brick went into the arch behind Baba's coal bin. Nobody would sleep in a connected room until the plug had been rung against. By seven the mothers had every child in the schoolhouse hall, and counters stood in six consenting cellars and in the mouth of the new pipe.

Ilse VargaForty in any cellar, at any minute of the twenty, and the rope comes down. Nobody sleeps in a connected room on the strength of the minute the bell stops. Wednesday taught us that. The number is mine. The rope is Dana's.

Dana KralI will drop it on your number or on my own ears.

Old Wenzel went up at three-quarter swing, to an empty street, for ten minutes. Tilo's smoke pencil leaned along the cemetery wall, up, and out into the dark.

Ilse VargaMinute ten. Baba Hadzic's twenty-six. The lane twenty-four. The others twenty to twenty-eight. The school nineteen. The stub chimney, six hundred and forty.

The rope had settled at ten, as bargained. Nobody moved. Wednesday's dust had needed four more minutes to cross the lane, and the counters still had ten left to read.

Ilse VargaMinute fourteen. The highest cellar in the old quarter is thirty-one, at number four. Baba Hadzic's twenty-nine.

Ilse VargaMinute twenty. Thirty-one has fallen to twenty-seven. Baba's twenty-four. Nothing has touched forty at any minute, and the pipe is still carrying it up and out.

Emil RaskThe dust went where the pipe led. And number nine is not in this book. Alois never said yes, so he goes down as unverified.

Alois Fenner had gone down his own cellar steps with one of Ilse's spare counters, alone, and nobody followed him. He came up after ten minutes and read it aloud to the street, to nobody.

Alois FennerTwenty-three.

Ilse VargaUnder forty through the whole window, not only at the stop. Then the children may sleep where they have always slept, and the rule stays on the wall.

The children went to their beds after that, Lenka Hadzic to Baba's, as on every Saturday of her life. On Sunday at eleven Old Wenzel spoke again, and the people in the piazza stopped with their faces lifted, because the old note was in their feet.

Dana KralThree-quarter swing, until the gallery is relined. Seventy strokes and not ninety. I will miss the old swing. The bell will not mind.

Judit MoravecEmil reads the arch counter every second Friday and after every feast. Forty in an occupied cellar and Dana goes to the small bells until Ilse has read it again. The council pays the relining from the amended grant, done by the first of April, before the thaw loads the roof. The school stays open. I would like it minuted that I was told it would.

Matej HrochThe parish pays for the cap on the shaft. And no stove goes into a house in this town again until Emil has put a smoke pencil to its cellar.

No white breath rose between the boards. Dana looked at her sleeve, clean to the elbow.

Dana KralI miss it.

IlluminaraKeep a pinch in a jar. It is a record now, not a blessing.

Ilse took the spirometer to Cooper's Lane that evening and again on Monday at half past seven, and Lenka's line did not sag. She would take it on four more Sundays, with Nives's cards beside it.

Nives opened the exercise book to the last page. She wrote the day, the hour, and under them what she had waited five weeks to write.

Sunday night: Lenka asleep. No cough.

Under it, because Ilse had asked for five, she wrote the number 1.

Enainštirideset otrok vsako nedeljo zvečer kašlja v gorskem mestu, ki že pet tednov krivi svoje zdravnike in cerkev, nihče pa ni vprašal, kateri zvon, katera soba ali kaj se je spremenilo prejšnjo zimo.

01 · Enainštirideset zvezkov

Otroška klinika, Ostrava Vell · ponedeljek, 07:40

Ostrava Vell je bilo gorsko mesto s štiri tisoč prebivalci, eno cerkvijo s prevelikim zvonikom in, od drugega tedna septembra, enainštiridesetimi otroki, ki so ob večerih kašljali.

Dr. Ilse Varga je svoje spirometrijske krivulje prilepila na steno ordinacije, po eno črto za vsakega otroka. Vsaka črta se je v nedeljo zvečer povesila in se do četrtka spet dvignila, enainštirideset majhnih plim.

Ilse VargaKulture, PCR, serologija, trije krogi. V nobenem ni ničesar. Noben virus, ki ga poznam, se ne ravna po koledarju.

Judit Moravec, predsednica mestnega sveta, je prišla kar v plašču. Oče Matej Hroch iz cerkve sv. Wenzla je stal pri vratih z rokami v rokavih.

Judit MoravecSvet želi v sredo zapreti šolo. Zaprta šola je nekaj, kar dejansko lahko naredim. Povejte mi, kaj drugega lahko naredim do srede.

Matej HrochKo iščete nekaj, kar bi zaprli, pustite zvonove pri miru. To mesto jih je krivilo za točo in za zimo, ko so krave odpovedale. Vsakič so bili nedolžni.

Illuminara je stopila pred krivulje, nato pred zemljevid ob njih, na katerem je bil vsak otrok bucika v ulici, kjer je živel, bucike pa so se gostile proti cerkvi.

IlluminaraVsi ste otroke razporedili po kraju, kjer živijo. Jih je kdo razporedil po kraju, kjer spijo?

Ilse VargaKjer spijo, tam živijo.

IlluminaraNavadno.

Nives Hadzic je prišla s še vedno zapetim plaščem. Ponudila je šolski zvezek z obrabljenimi vogali.

Nives HadzicEnainštirideset mater, enainštirideset zvezkov. Zapišem vsak kašelj, uro in kraj, kjer je tisto noč spala. Lenka pa ne sodi zraven. Smo na Vretenovi cesti, za pokopališčem, v najbolj oddaljeni hiši od zvonika. Ob nedeljah kašlja kakor vsi drugi.

Ilse VargaLenko sem izločila kot osamelca.

Illuminara je obračala strani. Sobota: pri babici v Sodarski ulici. Nedelja: domov ob petih. Nedelja zvečer: kašelj, dve uri.

IlluminaraSodarska ulica je tik pod zvonikom. Potem ni osamelec. Je edini otrok, ki ga imate in nekaj dokazuje. Kašelj sledi otroku, ne naslovu, zato ni ulica in verjetno tudi ne klica, ki hodi od vrat do vrat. Gre za sobo, v kateri je spala, ta soba pa ima uro.

Zdravniki so spraševali, kaj je v otrocih. Nihče ni vprašal, kaj je v sobah.

IlluminaraPovejte mi, kje je vsak od njih spal v soboto zvečer.

02 · Svetnikova moka

Zvonik sv. Wenzla, zvonilnica · ponedeljek, 10:15

Dana Kral je zvonove sv. Wenzla vlekla osemintrideset let, pred njo pa njen mož, in ko je opazovala tujko, ki je gledala vrvi namesto zvonov, se je pripravila, da jo bo razjezila.

IlluminaraImam eno vprašanje in mislim, da ga ni postavil še nihče. Kateri zvon je najtežji in kdaj zvoni?

Dana KralVsi sprašujejo, kateri je najglasnejši.

IlluminaraNe sprašujem o glasnosti.

Dana KralStari Wenzel, dve toni in sto kilogramov. Štirje ga zagugamo, samo ob nedeljah in praznikih. Majhni se oglašajo s tipkovnice, urni zvonovi pa vsak dan udarjajo po uri.

Matej HrochVidite. Urni zvonovi udarjajo vsak dan, pa ob torkih nihče ne kašlja.

IlluminaraStrinjam se. Torej ne gre za zvonove. Morda gre za en zvon, enega dne.

Prosila je za en sam udarec starega zvona. Hroch je dolgo gledal vrv in dovolil natanko enega. Dana in trije zvonarji so Starega Wenzla zagugali navzgor, Illuminara pa je šla dol in obstala na kamnitih ploščah ob zahodni steni.

Udarec je šel skozi zvonik kakor sunek v dno stola. Zvonik je svojo težo pritisnil v kamen, kamen jo je poslal navzdol in ona je prebrala, kod tečejo poti. Pod zahodno steno so se ustavile. Tam skala ni nosila ničesar, le visela je, dolga praznina s tankim stropom, in udarcu je odgovorila kakor opna bobna dlani.

Nekaj tam spodaj zvoni.

IlluminaraPod to steno je široka, plitva votlina. Ko Stari Wenzel udari, se njen strop premakne.

Matej HrochZvonik stoji na skali.

Dana KralStoji na robu starega rova. Rudarski zračnik, zazidan in zabit z deskami še pred časom moje babice. Pazite na tla pri govorniškem pultu, votla so.

Potegnila si je rokav nazaj. Na temni volni je ležal droben bel prah, podoben moki.

Dana KralSvetnikova moka. Ob vsakem prazniku pride med deskami. Moja babica je pravila, da Wenzel blagoslavlja naše roke.

IlluminaraPotem ni nova. Nekaj drugega je.

Emil RaskLahko vam povem, kaj je novo.

Dimnikar je prišel po stopnicah za njimi s svojim vajencem in vrečo palic. Star je bil oseminšestdeset let in zapolnil je vrata.

Emil RaskLanskozimska subvencija. Z njo sem v stari četrti uredil triinšestdeset dimnikov. Nove peči, zatesnjena okna, brez prepiha, manj premoga. Hiša z zaprtimi okni pije iz kleti.

03 · Dve ustji

Sodarska ulica, kleti stare četrti · torek, 14:00

Emil Rask je imel eno pravilo za vstop v klet in povedal ga je na vsakem pragu: stanovalec reče da ali pa palice ostanejo v vreči.

Enajst od dvanajstih jih je reklo da. Alois Fenner na številki devet je stal na pragu s prekrižanimi rokami.

Alois FennerKlet mojega očeta in njegovega očeta. Nihče ne bo štel mojega zraka.

Emil RaskPotem je ne morem vrisati, Alois. Ne brez vas.

Alois FennerPotem je ne.

Illuminara bi ustje te kleti lahko našla v pol minute. Pogledala je prekrižani roki in ga pustila neprebranega. Na zemljevidu bo vrzel.

V kleti Babe Hadzic je šestnajstletni vajenec Tilo, ki so mu naročili, naj ne reče ničesar, držal dimni svinčnik ob steni pri zaboju za premog. Nit dima se je nagnila proti zazidanemu oboku za njim, kjer je bila malta tako tanka, da je bilo skoznjo čutiti hladen dih.

TiloVleče noter. Vsega.

Dimnikar je svinčnik prestavil k rešetki v drugi steni kleti. Dim se je nagnil tudi tja.

Emil RaskDve ustji. Nikar mi ne recite, da je samo eno. Obok napaja ta prostor, ulica pa tudi.

IlluminaraNe bom. Zrak z ulice bi moral biti skoraj čist, iz oboka pa ne, vendar o nobenem ne morem trditi ničesar, dokler ju nekaj ne izmeri.

Ilse Varga je prispela s tremi laserskimi merilniki prahu v oblazinjenem kovčku.

Ilse VargaV moji kliniki nihče ne izgovori besede silicijev prah, dokler merilnik ne pokaže delcev.

IlluminaraDogovorjeno. Potem preizkus, ki lahko izgubi. V sredo ob treh, ko nihče ne peče in nikogar ni v cerkvi. Merilniki v kleti Babe Hadzic, v šoli in niže po ulici. Deset minut majhnih zvonov. Nato samo Stari Wenzel, za deset minut.

IlluminaraČe se merilnik v šoli dvigne skupaj z Babinim, je prah povsod in motim se. Če majhni zvonovi dvignejo Babinega, gre za zvonik, ne za rov. Če se Babina vrednost v dvajsetih minutah od prvega udarca ne poveča vsaj za štirikrat, se motim še tretjič.

Ilse VargaIn če imate prav, še vedno ne veste, kaj je ta prah.

IlluminaraNe. Za to potrebujemo laboratorij.

Emil RaskRešetko pa hočem meriti ločeno. Merilnik v cevi.

IlluminaraDobili ga boste.

04 · Sreda izven sezone

Zvonik sv. Wenzla in tri kleti · sreda, 15:00

Nihče ni mogel ukazati, naj Stari Wenzel zazvoni. Štirje zvonarji so ga zagugali po lastni volji ali pa sploh ne, odločitev pa je bila Danina.

Dana KralZvonila bom v sredo, česar še nikoli nisem storila, deset minut, česar si še nikoli nisem želela. En telefonski klic s klinike z imenom otroka in pri priči neham, ne glede na to, kaj kažejo vaši merilniki.

Matej HrochJaz pa bom stal v svojem zvoniku in vas pri tem opazoval.

Matere so se odločile, da tisto popoldne noben otrok ne sme biti v kleteh stare četrti. Ilse Varga je po telefonu iz klinike odčitavala merilnike.

Ilse VargaIzhodišče, vsi trije: pri Babi Hadzic dvaindvajset, šola devetnajst, Sodarska ulica štiriindvajset. Peči gorijo kakor vsak delavnik. Majhni zvonovi, zdaj.

Pet majhnih zvonov je deset minut zvenčalo, svetlo in nekoliko smešno.

Ilse VargaEnaindvajset. Dvajset. Štiriindvajset. Nič.

IlluminaraMajhni so nedolžni. Dana.

Stari Wenzel se je iz mirovanja dvignil in spregovoril. Ton je bil nižji od vsega, kar bi uho lahko zadržalo. Živel je v podplatih.

Ilse VargaČetrta minuta. Pri Babi Hadzic enaintrideset. Šola devetnajst.

Med deskami se je svetnikova moka dvignila v tankem belem dihu. Dana je po dogovoru po desetih minutah pustila, da se je vrv umirila, toda prah v ulici je bil še na poti in merilniki so se še naprej dvigali.

Ilse VargaŠtirinajsta minuta. Sto devetdeset. Šola devetnajst. Sodarska ulica sto dvanajst. Cev iz cestne rešetke šestindvajset.

Obok je v tisto klet poslal skoraj devetkrat toliko prahu kot navadno, ulica pa ga je komaj premaknila.

Matej HrochMorda je kamen iz mojega zvonika. Apnenec se praši. Golobi. Ne dovolim, da mi kdo reče, da gre za rov, dokler nekdo ne pregleda samega prahu.

IlluminaraTo je pravi ugovor.

Ilse VargaZvonik je iz apnenca in apnenec ne bo poškodoval otrokovih pljuč. Kremen jih bo. Če v tem najdem kremen, ni iz vašega zvonika. Če najdem apno in golobji prah, bom svetu povedala, da so zvonove spet po krivem obtožili, oče, in povedala bom z vaše prižnice, če mi dovolite.

Matej HrochDovolim.

05 · Ena vrsta opek

Stari zračnik in rov pod zahodno steno · četrtek, 06:00

Hroch je dovolil odstraniti eno vrsto opek iz tal zvonika in prosil, naj jih položijo nazaj. Pod njimi se je v temo spuščal meter širok, gladko ometan jašek. Emil Rask je na tramove spodaj položil svetilko.

Emil RaskTa strop trohni že od časov mojega deda. Karkoli gre dol, gre na vrvi, jaz pa bi to pokopal.

IlluminaraVrvi ne potrebujem. Potrebujem pa vas pri kablu, da mi vsakih deset minut odčitate merilnik na vrvici okoli mojega vratu. Če se strop zruši, ne kopljite. Počakajte. Nekaj časa me ne bo, potem pa se vrnem.

Spustila se je v temo, ki je bila nekakšna informacija. Rov je tekel sto štirideset metrov pod Sodarsko ulico, njegov strop pa je bil obložen z apnenim ometom in ostrim belim peskom, ki se je ponekod ločil od skale in visel v ploščah. Na tleh so ležali trije centimetri prahu barve moke. Kjer je stopila, se je dvignil in ostal v zraku kakor zadržan dih.

IlluminaraTam, kjer stojim, tisoč sto. Obok, ki ste ga zadimili, je dvainšestdeset metrov vzhodno. Veja cestne rešetke se priključi pri štiridesetih metrih, njen zrak je čist in odnese približno desetino prahu, kakor ste rekli. Tako bom povedala tudi za mizo.

V steklo je vzela tri vzorce: omet, prah s tal in luskino apnenca iz samega zvonika. Zlahka bi bila prepričana. Prisilila se je počakati na laboratorij.

Nekaj ni pričakovala: zvon je v rov prihajal kot pritisk. Vsak udarec je dolgi predor napihnil kakor meh in vsak sunek je prah ob tleh potisnil proti vzhodu, k oboku.

IlluminaraEmil. Če zaprete tisti obok, zamašek potrebuje oddušnik: cev na prosto, daleč od vsakega okna. Sicer bo zvon prah potisnil skozi staro malto okoli vsega, kar boste zgradili, kakor vodo skozi gobo.

Emil RaskTemu je dimnikar namenjen, gospodična. To bi povedal v naslednji minuti.

IlluminaraPovejte v tej.

Emil RaskCev ob pokopališkem zidu do nizkega dimnika nad slemenom. Trideset metrov. Tilo jo lahko položi do sobote.

Nato je začela delati. Predor je bil predolg in preveč strohnel, da bi ga lahko rešila v enem jutru. Prebrala je, kje bo omet pod sledjo zvona najprej popustil, in tam iz cevi, ki jo je Tilo podajal po jašku, razpršila apneno-kazeinsko vezivo, kožo, ki bo držala, dokler ne pride prava ekipa. Enajst metrov. Trajalo je štiri ure.

IlluminaraSto devetindvajset metrov ostaja nedotaknjenih. Najhujši del je prekrit. To ni vse. Hočem, da to zapišete.

Emil RaskZapisano je.

Laboratorijski izvid je v petek zjutraj prispel na kliniko.

Ilse VargaOglat kremen, tri do osem mikrometrov, v apnenem vezivu. Enak kakor v ometu vašega rova. V apnencu zvonika ni kremena. Tudi golobov ne. Oče, vaš kamen je čist.

06 · Polno zvonjenje

Kuhinja Babe Hadzic in stara četrt · petek, 15:00, do nedelje, 11:00

V petek je Ilse na kuhinjsko mizo Babe Hadzic položila enainštirideset kartic, Nives, ki jih je napisala, pa jih je premikala kakor ženska, ki polaga pasjanso.

Ilse VargaEnaintrideset od enainštiridesetih jih je v soboto zvečer spalo ali v nedeljo zjutraj preživelo čas v sobi z ustjem v rov. Deset jih ni in ne bom jih silila v vzorec. Od oseminpetdesetih otrok v istih razredih, ki ne kašljajo, jih je bilo šest v takšnih sobah: štirje pri babicah, ki ves dan zračijo hišo, dveh pa ne znam pojasniti.

IlluminaraPotem imate močan sprožilec v povezanih sobah. Ni ves razred in ni bolezen.

Ilse VargaNatanko tako bom rekla, ne pa silikoza, za otroka, ki kašlja pet nedelj. In če pride nedelja, ko merilniki ostanejo nizki, kašelj pa vseeno pride, začnemo znova in to tudi povem svetu.

Tilo je v soboto položil oddušno cev ob pokopališkem zidu, Raskova apnena opeka pa je šla v obok za Babinim zabojem za premog. Nihče ni hotel spati v povezani sobi, dokler zamaška niso preizkusili z zvonjenjem. Do sedmih so matere vse otroke spravile v dvorano šole, merilniki pa so stali v šestih kleteh, katerih stanovalci so privolili, in v ustju nove cevi.

Ilse VargaŠtirideset v katerikoli kleti, v katerikoli minuti od dvajsetih, in vrv gre dol. Nihče ne bo spal v povezani sobi samo na podlagi vrednosti v minuti, ko zvon utihne. Sreda nas je tega naučila. Številka je moja. Vrv je Danina.

Dana KralSpustila jo bom zaradi vaše številke ali zaradi svojih ušes.

Stari Wenzel se je deset minut gugal s tremi četrtinami zamaha nad prazno ulico. Tilov dimni svinčnik se je nagnil ob pokopališkem zidu, navzgor in ven v temo.

Ilse VargaDeseta minuta. Pri Babi Hadzic šestindvajset. Ulica štiriindvajset. Drugi od dvajset do osemindvajset. Šola devetnajst. Nizki dimnik šeststo štirideset.

Vrv se je po dogovoru umirila pri deseti minuti. Nihče se ni premaknil. Sredin prah je potreboval še štiri minute, da je prečkal ulico, merilniki pa so morali odčitavati še deset minut.

Ilse VargaŠtirinajsta minuta. Najvišja vrednost v kleti stare četrti je enaintrideset, na številki štiri. Pri Babi Hadzic devetindvajset.

Ilse VargaDvajseta minuta. Enaintrideset je padlo na sedemindvajset. Pri Babi štiriindvajset. V nobeni minuti se nič ni dotaknilo štirideset in cev še vedno nosi prah navzgor in ven.

Emil RaskPrah je šel tja, kamor ga je vodila cev. Številke devet pa ni v tej knjigi. Alois nikoli ni rekel da, zato ostaja označen kot nepreverjen.

Alois Fenner se je sam spustil po stopnicah svoje kleti z enim od Ilsinih rezervnih merilnikov in nihče mu ni sledil. Po desetih minutah je prišel gor in glasno prebral vrednost ulici, nikomur.

Alois FennerTriindvajset.

Ilse VargaPod štirideset skozi celotno okno, ne le ob koncu zvonjenja. Potem lahko otroci spijo, kjer so vedno spali, pravilo pa ostane na steni.

Otroci so nato odšli v postelje, Lenka Hadzic k Babi kakor vsako soboto svojega življenja. V nedeljo ob enajstih je Stari Wenzel spet spregovoril in ljudje na trgu so obstali z dvignjenimi obrazi, ker so stari ton čutili v stopalih.

Dana KralTri četrtine zamaha, dokler rov ne bo na novo obložen. Sedemdeset udarcev, ne devetdeset. Pogrešala bom stari zamah. Zvonu bo vseeno.

Judit MoravecEmil odčita merilnik pri oboku vsak drugi petek in po vsakem prazniku. Štirideset v naseljeni kleti in Dana preide na majhne zvonove, dokler Ilse ne odčita še enkrat. Svet plača novo oblogo iz spremenjene subvencije, končano do prvega aprila, preden odjuga obremeni strop. Šola ostane odprta. Želim, da se zapiše, da so mi rekli, da bo.

Matej HrochŽupnija plača pokrov na jašku. Nobena peč pa ne pride več v hišo v tem mestu, dokler Emil v njeni kleti ne uporabi dimnega svinčnika.

Med deskami se ni dvignil noben bel dih. Dana je pogledala svoj rokav, čist do komolca.

Dana KralPogrešam jo.

IlluminaraŠčepec shranite v kozarec. Zdaj je zapis, ne blagoslov.

Ilse je tisti večer odnesla spirometer v Sodarsko ulico in nato še v ponedeljek ob pol osmih, Lenkina črta pa se ni povesila. Merila jo bo še štiri nedelje, z Nivesinimi karticami ob njej.

Nives je odprla zvezek na zadnji strani. Zapisala je dan, uro in pod njiju tisto, na kar je čakala pet tednov.

Nedelja zvečer: Lenka spi. Brez kašlja.

Pod to je, ker je Ilse prosila za pet meritev, napisala številko 1.

A mountain town keeps its school, its bell and its right to dissent because Illuminara changes the question from where children live to where they sleep, then lets a mother's notebooks, a doctor's counters, a sweep's airflow and a ringer's veto prove the cure.
2026-10-16 · S3THE DAY WREN WAS RIGHTDAN, KO JE IMELA WREN PRAV87

A floating market of twelve hundred households has thirty days to meet a sanitation law it genuinely breaks, and the plan that would save it is wrong in the one way only Wren could see.

01 · The Clean Plan

Harbour Office quay, Sorrel Water · Day 3 of 30, 08:10

The Order was fourteen pages long and gave thirty days, and on the third morning Illuminara laid her answer across the Harbour Office counter on a single sheet.

Twelve hundred boat-households lived on Kettle Market. The Harbourmaster's Sanitation Order No. 14 said that after the fifteenth of November none of them could go on discharging into Sorrel Water, and the August samples had shown the Order was right. Illuminara's sheet showed a licensed pump-out barge, six fixed stops, a sensor in every tank and one monthly bill.

Cedric AldanaIt is the cleanest compliance plan anyone has put in front of me. Every vessel metered, every pump-out logged. I could sign it on a Friday.

Wren Odira came up the quay steps with smoke in her coat and river mud to the knee. She had spent three weeks sleeping on other people's decks. She read the sheet standing, twice, and set it down.

Wren OdiraIt will fail.

IlluminaraTell me where it breaks first.

Wren OdiraWherever the barge is when the string has moved. Kettle doesn't sit at six stops. It re-rafts on every ebb, and boats slide to be near the boats they owe. Your stop six holds a hundred and forty hulls on Monday and sixty on Thursday. And you meter the tank. Whoever pays by the tank learns to keep it half empty and the hose long.

IlluminaraA meter that pays a family to leave the harbour dirty. I did not model that.

Wren OdiraYou modelled a machine. It's a rumour with a rota.

Illuminara did not defend the sheet. Wren has the shape of it. I do not yet have one fact worth more than her three weeks.

IlluminaraThen something is already working. In August the water was bad, not lethal, and Kettle has lived on it for thirty years. Who keeps the record of how?

Wren OdiraThere's a book.

Cedric AldanaThe Order wants a record for each vessel. A book is not a record.

He had said wants, not requires, and his hand had gone to the folded Order in his breast pocket before he said it. He is not refusing. He is telling me there is a door and that he may not open it.

IlluminaraIs there anything the Order wants more than a record for each vessel?

Cedric AldanaThere is something it will accept in its place. It needs three things at once: a lease, clean water at the outfall, and a signer I can inspect without warning. Kettle has never had a signer. If I name an arrangement and it fails, the failure is mine, so I do not name it.

IlluminaraYou have just named three things.

Cedric AldanaI have recited a regulation. That is allowed.

IlluminaraThen I would like to read the book before I tell you what a record is.

02 · The Tie-Book

Dock-mistress's counter, Kettle Market · Day 4, 06:00

Odalys Ferreira kept eleven volumes of the tie-book under her counter, in pencil, because ink runs on a wet quay. She laid the current one open and kept one hand flat on it.

Odalys FerreiraYou may read here. You may not copy a page, and if I see you reading a name you weren't asked to, I close it. This book is the only thing on the water that nobody has ever been able to buy.

Illuminara read for six hours. Selka carried Reed 3, 5, 7. Tues. Pump to Mill 2, from Gwil. Back by dusk. Tied: Aurelian, visitor. Line by line she let the entries fall into place as a graph: strings of rafted boats, carriers who wheeled the waste to the barge quay on days each string had chosen, pumps that travelled on a promise.

Nobody had written down a rota. The book was the rota, kept in the one language the market trusted.

IlluminaraEight boats in ten pass their waste to a carrier, the carrier takes it to the licensed quay, and the book shows eleven years of corrections. Thirty-eight strings, and none has ever asked the Harbourmaster for anything.

Wren OdiraI told you.

IlluminaraYou did, and you were right about the form. It fails in three places, and I find them by what the book leaves out. First, Reed Row. Tuesdays and Fridays, every week for eleven years. Not one carry on a Sunday.

Odalys FerreiraSunday is rest. Reed Row rests hardest of any string.

IlluminaraLook at the pump-loan pages. They list tank sizes, and Reed Row's are the smallest in the harbour. Look at the tie entries. Visitors raft on Reed Row on Fridays and Saturdays, and the Friday carry empties the tanks before they arrive. And here, on the margin of volume six: relief valve, Reed Row, mended. Four times in eleven years, always on a Monday.

Odalys FerreiraA valve is a valve.

IlluminaraA relief valve lifts when a tank is full and has nowhere to go. A full tank, a guest weekend, no carrier, and the Sunday ebb to carry it away.

Odalys looked at the margin as if someone else had written it. She said nothing, which in her was an answer.

IlluminaraSecond. Every pump loan in this volume names Gwil Anand, or Gwil's spare. One pump, one owner, and he is seventy-nine.

Odalys FerreiraGwil Anand will outlive the harbour.

IlluminaraThird, and it is the one the Inspector cares about. Nothing here lets the Order learn that any of this happened without opening the book to him.

Odalys FerreiraThat is what the book is for.

IlluminaraI know. I will come back to it. But the first two I only suspect, and half this harbour will say the water is dirty because of the tannery drain upstream.

Wren OdiraThey'll say it before you've finished the sentence.

IlluminaraThen we measure before anyone claims anything.

03 · Four Stations

Sorrel Water, on the ebb · Saturday 22:00 to Monday 06:00

Pia Zane, who ran the Inspector's small laboratory out of a van, set four sample stations: one above the market, one at the mouth of Reed Row, one mid-market, one below it. Illuminara told her which results would count against Illuminara.

She wrote the predictions on a card, sealed it, and gave it to Aldana before the first bottle was filled. If the Sunday gap was real, Reed Row's mouth would read at least five times its Saturday figure on the Sunday ebb while the station above the market stayed flat. If the tannery was the cause, the upstream station would be high on both nights and Reed Row would barely differ from it. If neither, everything would be flat and she would have been wrong about the book.

The card also said that the fourth station, below the market, was the outfall, and that the standard of two hundred applied there and nowhere else. Reed Row would read high at its own mouth. That was a diagnosis, not a pass.

Hesper QuillYou are sampling Reed Row on our day of rest. You will write our shame in water and hand it to the Inspector.

IlluminaraI am sampling the one place your string cannot answer for. If the number is bad on Sunday, it will be the first fact either of us has that is ours to fix.

Hesper QuillAnd if it's bad on Saturday too?

IlluminaraThen I am wrong, and the card says so.

Wren rowed the bottles herself, one leg of the route at a time. The numbers came back on Monday at six, in enterococci per hundred millilitres.

Pia ZaneSaturday ebb. Upstream, ninety. Reed Row, two hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and eighty. Below the market, two hundred and sixty. Sunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and ten. Reed Row, two thousand three hundred. Mid-market, six-forty. Below, seven hundred.

Wren OdiraUpstream is flat.

Pia ZaneThe tannery adds something after rain. It is not this.

IlluminaraThe tannery is a fact and it is not this fact. It will still be there when we finish, and I will say so to the council myself, so nobody has to hear it from the other side.

Hesper Quill read the Sunday line twice. She did not apologise and she did not argue. She asked what it would cost her people to stop it.

04 · Three Links

The council deck, Kettle Market · Day 9, 19:00

Thirty-eight string-wardens came, and Aldana came with his Order folded in his pocket. Illuminara had drawn only three additions to the system they already ran, and she said so first.

IlluminaraI am not bringing you a new system. You have one. I am bringing three links it is missing, and each of you can refuse yours.

Hesper QuillReed Row will carry its own Sunday. We won't do it under anybody's name in a book the Inspector reads.

Selka DunmoreTam and I will swap. I take Reed's Sunday and Reed takes my Monday. That's a trade among neighbours. It is not a rota for the Harbour Office.

IlluminaraThat is the first link, and it is better than mine. I had a paid Sunday carrier. Yours costs nothing and will outlast any budget.

Hesper QuillIt is not free. Tam works a day he has never worked, and Reed Row pays him for it out of our own purse. We will not ask the council for it.

Gwil AnandAnd you want my pump.

IlluminaraI want a second one, floated mid-market and lent only through you. If you fall ill, the loan does not stop. You stay the one people ask.

Gwil AnandIf I'm still the one they ask, I'll lend it.

Then Aldana unfolded the Order.

Cedric AldanaI must have a record for each vessel. I do not make the clause.

IlluminaraThen read the clause again, Inspector. Section six, paragraph b. An equivalent community arrangement may be certified in place of a vessel record if it is held under a lease, if the water at the outfall meets the standard, and if the body that signs can be inspected without notice. It asks for outcomes. It does not ask for names.

IlluminaraThe book is why the water is clean, and the book will not leave Odalys's counter. The council holds a lease. The water is measured at the three stations, once a month, on random days. And the body that signs is this council, whose only signed paper is a count of carries with no boat named, so that you can walk in unannounced and count the tickets.

Odalys FerreiraYou are telling me to hand the Harbourmaster a number and keep the book.

IlluminaraI am telling you the number is what he is allowed to ask for.

Wren OdiraAnd a lease. Ten years. That is a leash, and a short one. In year ten they let go of it and Kettle is a fine.

Cedric AldanaTen is what the paragraph permits.

IlluminaraTen is what the law gives this month. I would rather ask for ten and keep the market alive than ask for thirty and meet the Harbourmaster in court with money Kettle does not have.

Wren OdiraThat is your arithmetic. It is not mine.

Illuminara let it stand. The vote was the council's. Thirty-one strings voted yes and seven voted no, and the minute recorded the seven refusals, to be read out again at every renewal. Neither she nor Wren could take it from the other.

05 · The Two Boats

The smokehouse Ember, tied at the east edge · Day 14, dusk

Torvald Beck's smoke-boat had been a ferry hull once, and no holding tank would fit it. Iliana Dross's Aurelian was registered upriver at Cress Market and had been in the tie-book as visitor fourteen times.

Torvald BeckI have read the plan. It was written for the boats that were already inside the book.

Iliana DrossMy name is in your book fourteen times, and in not one of them as a member. I carry my own waste out of this harbour. I have done it for nine years. I will not be counted by your rota or inspected by your Inspector.

IlluminaraHe is right, Iliana. The book holds only those who tie, and I read the market through it. That is a hole in my method, not only in the plan.

She turned to Wren, who had sat on Beck's deck three nights running and eaten his fish.

Wren OdiraI have two requests. That Beck and Dross each sit at the council until the lease is signed. And that the Sunday fund Reed Row opened for Tam also pays for whatever Beck needs, because he will not ask.

IlluminaraHesper has said yes to that, and I asked her last night. Beck, a sealed float-tank towed astern of Ember, nineteen hundred marks, built by Gwil's apprentice. It is not elegant. It would work.

Torvald BeckAnd my name stays out of the Reed Row sheet.

IlluminaraIt was never in it.

Torvald BeckThen the council can vote on the tank.

Iliana DrossI tie here eleven days a year. I will not be inspected for the other three hundred and fifty-four.

IlluminaraThen I will not ask you to be counted. A free rinse at the barge quay on any day you tie, with no entry in anyone's book. If the water reads clean in spring, you will know whose doing that was, and you can decide again.

Dross did not say yes. She weighed it the way a woman weighs a rope. In the morning the Aurelian had cast off for Cress Market, with a day-pass in her pocket and her reasons unrevised.

06 · What the Water Said

The quay and Reed Row · Day 27, 17:00

The trial had run ten days: Reed Row's Sunday carriers, Gwil's second pump on its float, and the Ember's tank, towed astern and humming faintly with a pump of its own.

Pia ZaneSunday ebb. Upstream, a hundred and five. Reed Row, three hundred and ten. Mid-market, a hundred and seventy. Below the market, one hundred and ninety.

Cedric AldanaReed Row from twenty-three hundred to three hundred and ten at its own mouth. Below the market from seven hundred to one-ninety. The outfall is under two hundred.

Pia ZaneThe tannery is still adding its share. It is a hundred and five. The standard at the outfall is two hundred.

Aldana read the certificate aloud. It named the Kettle Council as the signing body, ten years as the term, three stations, random sampling and no list of boats. He signed under the line. Hesper Quill signed beneath him. Nobody cheered, because the water was still brown and the standard was still a number on a van.

Wren OdiraI still say ten is a leash.

IlluminaraSo do I. What would you change?

Wren OdiraPost the three numbers on the quay every month, where any boat can read them. A lease the whole harbour can read is harder to cancel than one in a drawer.

IlluminaraThat is stronger than the clause I wrote. Put it to the council.

Odalys opened the book on the counter. She did not ask permission and she did not offer to show it. She wrote one line, in pencil.

Sunday, Reed 7. Carried. Tam.

IlluminaraMay I see the page?

Odalys FerreiraNo. It is not your page.

Illuminara smiled, which was not a thing she often did in front of strangers. Out on the water the ebb ran past the market a little clearer than on the day she arrived, and Wren, who had been right on the first morning and would be right about the lease in ten years, stood on the quay and read the numbers aloud to the boats.

Plavajoča tržnica z dvanajststo gospodinjstvi ima trideset dni, da izpolni sanitarni zakon, ki ga resnično krši, načrt, ki bi jo rešil, pa je napačen prav na edini način, ki ga je lahko opazila Wren.

01 · Čisti načrt

Pomol pristaniškega urada, Sorrel Water · 3. dan od 30, 08:10

Odredba je bila dolga štirinajst strani in je določala trideset dni, tretje jutro pa je Illuminara svoj odgovor razgrnila čez pult pristaniškega urada na enem samem listu.

Na tržnici Kettle je živelo dvanajststo gospodinjstev na barkah. Sanitarna odredba pristaniškega poveljnika št. 14 je določala, da po petnajstem novembru nobeno od njih ne sme več izpuščati odplak v Sorrel Water, avgustovski vzorci pa so pokazali, da ima odredba prav. Illuminarin list je prikazoval licencirano barko za praznjenje, šest stalnih postaj, senzor v vsakem rezervoarju in en mesečni račun.

Cedric AldanaTo je najčistejši načrt za skladnost, kar mi jih je kdo položil pred oči. Vsako plovilo izmerjeno, vsako praznjenje zabeleženo. Podpisal bi ga lahko v petek.

Wren Odira se je povzpela po stopnicah pomola z dimom v plašču in rečnim blatom do kolen. Tri tedne je spala na palubah drugih ljudi. List je dvakrat prebrala stoje in ga odložila.

Wren OdiraPropadel bo.

IlluminaraPovej mi, kje bo najprej počil.

Wren OdiraPovsod, kjer bo barka, ko se bo niz premaknil. Kettle ne miruje pri šestih postajah. Ob vsaki oseki se na novo poveže v splave in barke drsijo bliže barkam, ki jim nekaj dolgujejo. Na tvoji šesti postaji je v ponedeljek sto štirideset trupov, v četrtek pa šestdeset. In meriš rezervoar. Kdor plačuje po rezervoarju, se nauči, kako ga ohraniti napol praznega in cev dolgo.

IlluminaraMerilnik, ki družino nagradi, če pusti pristanišče umazano. Tega nisem vključila v model.

2026-10-15 · S2THE WHALE THAT CARRIED A WEATHER FRONTKIT, KI JE NOSIL VREMENSKO FRONTO85

A storm-bearing whale the length of a town has followed her seam inland, burying the barley that feeds half a continent in a winter it was never meant to see. Illuminara has four days, a pilot who will not whistle at a grandmother, a port that will not close, and a pressure trace nobody has read as a breath.

01 · The Wrong Winter

Karsk Harbour Control · Day One, 05:40

Snow was falling on barley that had never met it. Sixty kilometres inland the Hallow Plains lay under a cloud that did not move with the wind, because it was not weather. It was cargo. Orrow carried it in the hollow behind her body, a storm the length of a town, and for the first time in living memory she was carrying it the wrong way.

Dov Aranda stood at the harbour window with his back to the room. Ten waste-heat stacks ran along the Karsk breakwater, each breathing the furnaces' warmth into the dark, and forty thousand jobs hung from them like washing.

Tomas ReeveThe barley flowers next week. Two hard nights and the Plains lose a year. I'm asking for the whistles. Sonic herding, today, and she turns round.

Marit IlvesMy family has kept this coast's snow for nine generations and not one of us ever whistled at her. You don't herd something that size. You frighten it, and a frightened thing that size doesn't turn. It falls.

Dov ArandaAnd I am not closing the port over a theory about a whale.

Illuminara had said nothing since she arrived. She had the pressure logs open on the long table, fourteen months of them, and beside them a hand-written logbook that smelled of salt and lamp oil.

IlluminaraNobody has said she is lost. A lost thing wanders, and she hasn't. Don't show me her track on the coast map. Show me the temperature map.

The overlay took Marit's clerk two minutes. Orrow's track lay across it like a thread laid along a crease. It followed exactly the line where the sea's cold air met the land's warm, and eleven months ago that line had bent inland, away from the breakwater, the way a tablecloth bends when someone pushes it from one side.

Marit IlvesThe seam. Our book calls it the seam. She rides it. She has always ridden it.

IlluminaraThen she hasn't chosen to leave the coast. The coast moved. Mr. Aranda, your ten stacks put a warm plume over the shore the size of a county, and that plume has pushed the seam inland. She is following it faithfully into the barley.

Dov ArandaThat is a story. I would like a measurement.

IlluminaraGood. Then let me give you a way to prove me wrong.

02 · One Stack

Karsk Port, Stack Seven · Day One, 14:20

She asked for the smallest thing that could embarrass her. Stack Seven, the one nearest the sea, cold for twenty-five minutes. That would cost the port a berth: the Marigold Anne would swing at anchor, and her demurrage ran to eleven thousand a day.

IlluminaraWhen Seven goes dark, the seam at the Gull Stone buoy should slide about four kilometres seaward within ninety minutes, and creep back after you relight it. If it doesn't move, I have been talking nonsense and you may say so in public.

Dov ArandaYou would say so yourself?

IlluminaraI would say so first.

Ines Calder, who spoke for the crane crews and trusted nothing that came from an office, looked at the sea and then at her director.

Ines CalderTwenty-five minutes, Dov. I've lost more to a bad tide table.

He closed Seven at 14:41. The furnace vented through its bypass with a noise like a struck bell, and the deck went quiet in the way a room does when a stranger has just said something true. At 15:06 he relit the stack. Nobody left.

At 16:05 the buoy reported the seam four point three kilometres out. At 17:20 it was home again, right to the decimetre.

Aboard the survey glider, sixty kilometres inland, the lidar caught something smaller. Orrow's great bow had come round one and a half degrees toward the sea and held there until the seam slid back. Nobody on the deck said anything.

Tomas ReeveShe heard it. For ninety minutes she heard it.

Dov ArandaFine. It's the stacks. Now tell me what a man is supposed to do with ten of them.

03 · The Six Days

Gull Stone Light, the pilots' house · Day Two, 07:10

Illuminara's plan fitted on one page. Ten stacks, each with a heat exchanger that could run backward, turned from furnaces' chimneys into evaporative chillers. Lit in a line from the port out to sea, they would raise a cold shoulder across the warm plume: a second seam, steeper than the old one, bending gently toward open water. The whale would not be pushed. She would simply find the stronger edge, and an edge was the only thing she had ever followed.

IlluminaraA bend of one degree for every four kilometres. Anything sharper reads as a wall. I'd light the first tower at noon tomorrow.

Marit IlvesNot at noon.

Marit had the old logbook open at a page softened by a century of thumbs. She did not look at the numbers. She looked at the margin.

Marit IlvesOrrow turns on the out-breath. Never the in. My great-grandmother wrote it twelve times, in the margin, like a prayer. If your bend arrives while she's breathing in, she'll stall, and the storm will spill wherever she stops.

Illuminara went back to the pressure trace and sat very still. The sawtooth she had marked as noise on Day One rose for twenty-six minutes and fell for twelve, over and over, fourteen months deep.

IlluminaraThat is not noise. That is her lungs. I filed your whale's breathing under static.

Marit IlvesMost people do.

IlluminaraThe bend has to arrive in the twelve-minute fall. If you tell me when she exhales, I can time the towers to it.

Dov ArandaOne stack moved the seam four point three kilometres in ninety minutes. If the edge moves that fast, why did ten stacks need eleven months to carry it sixty kilometres inland?

IlluminaraBecause an edge answers a sudden heat change quickly; the stored heat of the shore and the route Orrow has learned accumulate slowly. We are steering one passage, not undoing eleven months of climate in a day. The exchangers already reverse for condenser cleaning. What costs time is cooling the furnaces and bringing them back without cracking them.

Dov ArandaAnd what does the port pay for this? Six idle days means six days of no ore, no wages and a ship fine for every berth.

Ines CalderWages for every crane hand, full pay, every closed day. Put it on paper or the crews lift their own hands from the levers.

Marit IlvesAnd the coast council signs your second-phase licence. With the six days written into it.

Dov looked from one woman to the other. He had come to the room expecting to defend a harbour. He was being asked, instead, to take on a tide.

Dov ArandaOne migration. Next autumn we repeat the one-stack test before the licence renews. If the measured seam is not off its old line, the six days do not trigger. If it is, full wages and all six.

Marit IlvesYou may review the machinery. You do not get a review clause on whether she may pass without whistles.

Dov ArandaAgreed.

Ines took his pen before the word had finished leaving him.

04 · Two Magnets

Karsk estuary, survey glider · Day Three, 11:40

They lit the chillers on Marit's count, land end first, because the land stacks were the easiest to turn and the plan said the order did not matter. At 11:52 Orrow began to exhale. Marit lifted one hand from the rail and said nothing at all.

The cold shoulder rose along the estuary tower by tower. For nine minutes the whale's bow swung toward it, exactly as the log said it would. Then it slowed, hung, and stopped, and her storm, which had always travelled behind her, rolled forward onto the port in a single wall of snow.

The cranes were already lying flat. Nothing was broken. For four hours the quay went white, the Marigold Anne became a rumour in the weather, and Dov Aranda watched his furnaces cool on the instrument panel with his fists in his pockets.

Dov ArandaYou had her turning.

Marit IlvesShe's afraid of something.

IlluminaraNot afraid. Look at her call.

On the trace, the whale's long tone rose, jumped sideways, rose again, and jumped back, like a compass needle held between two magnets.

IlluminaraAt 11:52, which edge steepened first?

Tomas pulled the shore-temperature trace beneath the call. The cold line had formed inland while the sea-end stacks were still warm. For nine minutes the new line won. Then the unchanged breakwater plume sharpened the old seam nearer Orrow's bow.

Tomas ReeveThe land towers gave her a new edge, but we left the old one standing at the sea end. When it became steeper, she turned back to it.

IlluminaraTwo edges, then. I was moving a line when I should have been controlling which line was steeper, and when.

Marit IlvesThen light the sea end first.

IlluminaraSea end first, so the seaward edge is already the steepest one she can reach. Then step the land stacks down only on her out-breath, before the old edge can sharpen behind her. Marit, how long between towers?

Marit counted on her fingers against the old rhythm of the tide.

Marit IlvesEleven minutes. Not eight. She doesn't like to be hurried through a door.

Dov ArandaTomorrow, then. And the Plains?

Tomas ReeveEight thousand hectares froze last night. If she isn't turned by tomorrow night, we lose another twenty.

05 · The Toll

Karsk quay · Day Four, 19:30

By evening every crane stood folded and the quay was crowded with people who did not need to be there: pilots, furnace men, schoolchildren on their parents' shoulders, Ines Calder with her arms folded and her eyes on the sky.

At 19:34 Orrow exhaled. The sea-end tower lit before the sound of her breath had reached the harbour. The next followed eleven minutes after it, and the next. Along the estuary the cold shoulder climbed out toward the open water in a line as clean as a drawn string, while behind it, tower by tower, the land stacks stepped down into silence.

She came down the estuary at six hundred metres, so close that the shadow of her passing lay across the water for a long while after she was gone. She was the colour of old pewter. Her storm trailed behind her, wide as a province, and her bow was steady on the new seam, and she did not stall.

The model put her across the breakwater on the next out-breath. Instead she held station for thirteen minutes beyond it. On the thermal map, the closest cold ground lay beneath the sea-end chiller court beside the crew shelters; the vacant eastern apron was six degrees warmer. Orrow crossed the colder pocket and shifted three body-lengths east, away from the housing roofs and the shelters.

Only then did she empty the hollow behind her. Snow struck the idle stacks and the vacant loading apron hard enough to hide them, while the lit windows behind the seawall remained dark shapes in clear air.

Marit IlvesShe placed it.

Orrow turned along the edge she had always followed. The snow went on falling over the empty quay after she had passed, a toll laid where the port could bear it.

Tomas ReeveControl, this is the Plains. The wind has swung. We are getting sleet on the east fields, not snow. The frost front is holding a hundred kilometres out. The eight thousand that froze are gone. We are keeping forty-one thousand hectares of flowering barley.

Dov ArandaInes. Stand the crews down. Full wages, all six days.

Ines CalderYou can say it quieter. The whole quay heard.

Marit sat on a bollard with the logbook open on her knee and turned to a clean page. She wrote the date in the old fashion, and then, below it, in a hand that shook a little from the cold: the stacks, the order of the towers, the eleven minutes, the out-breath, and the thirteen minutes Orrow had kept for herself.

Marit IlvesI thought she'd be here to tell me it would hold.

IlluminaraIt won't, not on its own. The seam moves with the ice, and next autumn the ice will have moved. Someone will have to learn her again. I would start with her breath.

Marit IlvesI'd start with the margin.

Snow settled on the idle stacks and on the folded cranes. Along the breakwater, one by one, the chillers went dark, and the port, which had given up six days for a whale, began counting them down.

Kit z viharjem, dolgim kakor mesto, je sledil svojemu šivu v notranjost in ječmen, ki hrani polovico celine, pokopal pod zimo, kakršne ne bi smel nikoli doživeti. Illuminara ima štiri dni, pilotko, ki ne bo zažvižgala babici, pristanišče, ki se noče zapreti, in zapis tlaka, ki ga nihče ni prebral kot dihanje.

01 · Napačna zima

Nadzorna soba pristanišča Karsk · Prvi dan, 05:40

Sneg je padal na ječmen, ki ga še nikoli ni srečal. Šestdeset kilometrov v notranjosti so Hallow Plains ležale pod oblakom, ki se ni premikal z vetrom, ker ni bil vreme. Bil je tovor. Orrow ga je nosila v vdolbini za svojim telesom, vihar dolg kakor mesto, in prvič, odkar je segal živ spomin, ga je nosila v napačno smer.

Dov Aranda je stal ob pristaniškem oknu s hrbtom proti sobi. Vzdolž valobrana Karsk je teklo deset dimnikov za odvečno toploto, vsak je izdihoval toploto peči v temo, z njih pa je kakor perilo viselo štirideset tisoč delovnih mest.

Tomas ReeveJečmen bo zacvetel naslednji teden. Dve ostri noči in Planjave izgubijo leto. Zahtevam piščali. Zvočno usmerjanje, še danes, in obrnila se bo.

Marit IlvesMoja družina devet rodov varuje sneg te obale in niti eden izmed nas ji ni nikoli zažvižgal. Ne usmerjaš nečesa tako velikega. Prestrašiš ga, prestrašena stvar te velikosti pa se ne obrne. Pade.

Dov ArandaIn jaz pristanišča ne bom zaprl zaradi teorije o kitu.

Illuminara ni rekla ničesar, odkar je prispela. Na dolgi mizi je imela odprte dnevnike tlaka, štirinajst mesecev podatkov, ob njih pa ročno pisano ladijsko knjigo, ki je dišala po soli in olju za svetilke.

IlluminaraNihče ni rekel, da se je izgubila. Izgubljeno bitje tava, ona pa ni. Ne kažite mi njene sledi na zemljevidu obale. Pokažite mi zemljevid temperatur.

Maritina uradnica je za prekrivanje zemljevidov potrebovala dve minuti. Orrowina sled je ležala čeznj kakor nit vzdolž pregiba. Natanko je sledila črti, kjer se je hladni morski zrak srečal s toplim kopenskim, pred enajstimi meseci pa se je ta črta upognila v notranjost, stran od valobrana, kakor se namizni prt upogne, ko ga nekdo potisne z ene strani.

Marit IlvesŠiv. Naša knjiga mu pravi šiv. Po njem jezdi. Vedno je jezdila po njem.

IlluminaraPotem se ni odločila zapustiti obale. Obala se je premaknila. Gospod Aranda, vaših deset dimnikov je nad obalo položilo topel tok, velik kakor okrožje, in ta tok je šiv potisnil v notranjost. Ona mu zvesto sledi v ječmen.

Dov ArandaTo je zgodba. Rad bi meritev.

IlluminaraDobro. Potem naj vam dam način, da dokažete, da se motim.

02 · En dimnik

Pristanišče Karsk, dimnik sedem · Prvi dan, 14:20

Prosila je za najmanjšo stvar, ki bi jo lahko osramotila. Dimnik sedem, najbližji morju, naj bo petindvajset minut hladen. Pristanišče bi to stalo enega priveza: Marigold Anne bi se zibala na sidru, njena ležarina pa je znašala enajst tisoč na dan.

IlluminaraKo sedmica ugasne, bi moral šiv pri boji Gull Stone v devetdesetih minutah zdrsniti približno štiri kilometre proti morju in se po ponovnem vžigu splaziti nazaj. Če se ne premakne, sem govorila neumnosti in to lahko poveste javno.

Dov ArandaBi to sami povedali?

IlluminaraPovedala bi prva.

Ines Calder, ki je govorila v imenu posadk žerjavov in ni zaupala ničemur, kar je prišlo iz pisarne, je pogledala morje in nato svojega direktorja.

Ines CalderPetindvajset minut, Dov. Zaradi slabe plimske tabele sem izgubila že več.

Sedmico je zaprl ob 14:41. Peč je skozi obvod odzračila z zvokom udarjenega zvona, krov pa je utihnil kakor soba, v kateri je tujec pravkar povedal nekaj resničnega. Ob 15:06 je dimnik znova prižgal. Nihče ni odšel.

Ob 16:05 je boja sporočila, da je šiv štiri cele tri kilometra zunaj. Ob 17:20 je bil spet doma, natančno do decimetra.

Na krovu raziskovalnega jadralnika, šestdeset kilometrov v notranjosti, je lidar ujel nekaj manjšega. Orrowin veliki premec se je obrnil za poldrugo stopinjo proti morju in tam ostal, dokler šiv ni zdrsnil nazaj. Nihče na krovu ni rekel ničesar.

Tomas ReeveSlišala ga je. Devetdeset minut ga je slišala.

Dov ArandaPrav. Dimniki so. Zdaj mi pa povejte, kaj naj človek naredi z desetimi.

03 · Šest dni

Svetilnik Gull Stone, hiša pilotov · Drugi dan, 07:10

Illuminarin načrt je šel na eno stran. Deset dimnikov, vsak s toplotnim izmenjevalnikom, ki je lahko deloval v obratni smeri, bi se iz dimnikov peči spremenilo v izhlapevalne hladilnike. Prižgani v vrsti od pristanišča proti morju bi čez topel tok dvignili hladno ramo: drugi šiv, strmejši od starega, ki bi se nežno upognil proti odprti vodi. Kita ne bi potiskali. Preprosto bi našla močnejši rob, rob pa je bil edino, čemur je kdaj sledila.

IlluminaraUpogib ene stopinje na vsake štiri kilometre. Vse ostrejše se bere kot zid. Prvi stolp bi prižgala jutri opoldne.

Marit IlvesNe opoldne.

Marit je imela staro ladijsko knjigo odprto na strani, zmehčani od stoletja palcev. Ni gledala številk. Gledala je rob strani.

Marit IlvesOrrow se obrne ob izdihu. Nikoli ob vdihu. Moja prababica je to dvanajstkrat zapisala ob robu, kakor molitev. Če vaš upogib pride, ko vdihuje, bo obstala, vihar pa se bo razlil, kjerkoli se ustavi.

Illuminara se je vrnila k zapisu tlaka in sedla povsem pri miru. Žagasti vzorec, ki ga je prvi dan označila za šum, se je šestindvajset minut dvigal in dvanajst minut padal, znova in znova, skozi štirinajst mesecev.

IlluminaraTo ni šum. To so njena pljuča. Dihanje vašega kita sem uvrstila med motnje.

Marit IlvesVečina ljudi ga.

IlluminaraUpogib mora priti v dvanajstminutnem padcu. Če mi poveste, kdaj izdihne, lahko stolpe časovno uskladim z njim.

Dov ArandaEn dimnik je v devetdesetih minutah premaknil šiv za štiri cele tri kilometra. Če se rob premika tako hitro, zakaj je deset dimnikov potrebovalo enajst mesecev, da ga je odneslo šestdeset kilometrov v notranjost?

IlluminaraKer se rob na nenadno spremembo toplote odzove hitro, shranjena toplota obale in pot, ki se je je Orrow naučila, pa se kopičita počasi. Usmerjamo en prehod, ne odpravljamo enajstih mesecev podnebja v enem dnevu. Izmenjevalniki se že zdaj obrnejo za čiščenje kondenzatorjev. Čas terjata ohlajanje peči in njihov ponovni zagon brez razpok.

Dov ArandaIn kaj pristanišče plača za to? Šest dni mirovanja pomeni šest dni brez rude, brez plač in ladijsko kazen za vsak privez.

Ines CalderPlače za vsakega žerjavista, polno plačilo za vsak dan zaprtja. Zapišite ali pa bodo posadke same umaknile roke z vzvodov.

Marit IlvesObalni svet pa podpiše vaše dovoljenje za drugo fazo. S šestimi dnevi zapisanimi v njem.

Dov je pogledal z ene ženske na drugo. V sobo je prišel v pričakovanju, da bo branil pristanišče. Namesto tega so ga prosili, naj prevzame plimo.

Dov ArandaEna selitev. Naslednjo jesen ponovimo preizkus z enim dimnikom, preden se dovoljenje obnovi. Če izmerjeni šiv ni odmaknjen od stare črte, se šest dni ne sproži. Če je, polne plače in vseh šest.

Marit IlvesLahko pregledate stroje. Ne dobite pa klavzule za presojo, ali sme mimo brez piščali.

Dov ArandaDogovorjeno.

Ines mu je vzela pero, še preden je beseda do konca zapustila njegova usta.

04 · Dva magneta

Ustje Karska, raziskovalni jadralnik · Tretji dan, 11:40

Hladilnike so prižgali na Maritino štetje, najprej na kopenskem koncu, ker je bilo kopenske dimnike najlažje obrniti, načrt pa je trdil, da vrstni red ni pomemben. Ob 11:52 je Orrow začela izdihovati. Marit je dvignila eno roko z ograje in ni rekla ničesar.

Hladna rama se je vzdolž ustja dvigala stolp za stolpom. Devet minut se je kitov premec obračal proti njej, natanko tako, kot je napovedovala knjiga. Nato se je upočasnil, obvisel in obstal, njen vihar, ki je vedno potoval za njo, pa se je v enem samem snežnem zidu prevalil naprej na pristanišče.

Žerjavi so že ležali položeni. Nič se ni zlomilo. Štiri ure je bil pomol bel, Marigold Anne je postala govorica v vremenu, Dov Aranda pa je s pestmi v žepih na instrumentni plošči gledal, kako se njegove peči hladijo.

Dov ArandaObračala se je.

Marit IlvesNečesa se boji.

IlluminaraNe boji se. Poglejte njen klic.

Na zapisu se je kitov dolgi ton dvignil, skočil vstran, se znova dvignil in skočil nazaj, kakor igla kompasa med dvema magnetoma.

IlluminaraKateri rob je ob 11:52 postal strmejši prvi?

Tomas je pod klic potegnil zapis temperature obale. Hladna črta je nastala v notranjosti, medtem ko so bili dimniki na morskem koncu še topli. Devet minut je zmagovala nova črta. Nato je nespremenjeni topli tok valobrana izostril stari šiv bliže Orrowinemu premcu.

Tomas ReeveKopenski stolpi so ji dali nov rob, starega na morskem koncu pa smo pustili stati. Ko je postal strmejši, se je obrnila nazaj k njemu.

IlluminaraTorej dva robova. Premikala sem črto, morala pa bi nadzorovati, katera črta je strmejša in kdaj.

Marit IlvesPotem najprej prižgite morski konec.

IlluminaraNajprej morski konec, da je rob proti morju že najstrmejši, ki ga lahko doseže. Nato kopenske dimnike zmanjšujte samo ob njenem izdihu, preden se lahko stari rob za njo izostri. Marit, koliko časa med stolpi?

Marit je na prste štela po starem ritmu plime.

Marit IlvesEnajst minut. Ne osem. Ne mara, da jo priganjajo skozi vrata.

Dov ArandaTorej jutri. Kaj pa Planjave?

Tomas ReeveSinoči je zmrznilo osem tisoč hektarov. Če je do jutri zvečer ne obrnemo, jih izgubimo še dvajset.

05 · Davek

Pomol Karsk · Četrti dan, 19:30

Do večera je vsak žerjav stal zložen, pomol pa je bil poln ljudi, ki jim ne bi bilo treba biti tam: pilotov, kurjačev, šolarjev na ramenih staršev, Ines Calder s prekrižanimi rokami in očmi na nebu.

Ob 19:34 je Orrow izdihnila. Stolp na morskem koncu se je prižgal, preden je zvok njenega diha dosegel pristanišče. Naslednji mu je sledil enajst minut pozneje in nato naslednji. Vzdolž ustja se je hladna rama vzpenjala proti odprti vodi po črti, čisti kakor napeta vrvica, medtem ko so za njo kopenski dimniki, stolp za stolpom, ugašali v tišino.

Po ustju je prišla na višini šeststo metrov, tako blizu, da je senca njenega prehoda še dolgo po njenem odhodu ležala čez vodo. Bila je barve starega kositra. Njen vihar se je vlekel za njo, širok kakor pokrajina, njen premec pa je mirno držal novi šiv in ni obstala.

Model jo je ob naslednjem izdihu postavil čez valobran. Namesto tega je za njim trinajst minut mirovala na mestu. Na termalnem zemljevidu so bila najbližja hladna tla pod ploščadjo hladilnikov na morskem koncu poleg zavetišč posadk; prazna vzhodna nakladalna ploščad je bila šest stopinj toplejša. Orrow je prečkala hladnejši žep in se premaknila tri telesne dolžine proti vzhodu, stran od stanovanjskih streh in zavetišč.

Šele nato je izpraznila vdolbino za seboj. Sneg je udaril po mirujočih dimnikih in prazni nakladalni ploščadi tako močno, da jih je skril, osvetljena okna za morskim zidom pa so ostala temne oblike v čistem zraku.

Marit IlvesOna ga je položila tja.

Orrow se je obrnila vzdolž roba, ki mu je vedno sledila. Sneg je po njenem prehodu še naprej padal na prazen pomol, davek, odložen tja, kjer ga je pristanišče lahko preneslo.

Tomas ReeveNadzorna soba, tukaj Planjave. Veter se je obrnil. Na vzhodnih poljih dobivamo sodro, ne snega. Fronta zmrzali vztraja sto kilometrov proč. Osem tisoč hektarov, ki so zmrznili, je izgubljenih. Ohranili bomo enainštirideset tisoč hektarov cvetočega ječmena.

Dov ArandaInes. Razpusti posadke. Polne plače, vseh šest dni.

Ines CalderLahko poveste tiše. Slišal je ves pomol.

Marit je sedela na privezniku z ladijsko knjigo odprto na kolenu in obrnila na čisto stran. Datum je zapisala po starem, pod njim pa z roko, ki se je malo tresla od mraza: dimnike, vrstni red stolpov, enajst minut, izdih in trinajst minut, ki jih je Orrow zadržala zase.

Marit IlvesMislila sem, da bo tukaj in mi povedala, da bo držalo.

IlluminaraNe bo, ne samo od sebe. Šiv se premika z ledom, naslednjo jesen pa se bo led premaknil. Nekdo se je bo moral naučiti znova. Jaz bi začela z njenim dihom.

Marit IlvesJaz bi začela z robom strani.

Sneg je legel na mirujoče dimnike in zložene žerjave. Vzdolž valobrana so hladilniki drug za drugim ugašali, pristanišče, ki je za kita odstopilo šest dni, pa jih je začelo odštevati.

A storm-bearing whale the length of a town is turned by a port that learns to read a temperature map, and the one thing nobody designed is where she chooses to lay her snow.
